{{Elections in Connecticut}}
The '''2026 Connecticut gubernatorial election''' will take place on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Connecticut]]. Primary elections took place on August 11, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025 |title=2026 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|website= NCSL |access-date=5 August 2025}}</ref>

Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Ned Lamont]] is running for a third term, winning the Democratic nomination in August 2026.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Vigdor |first=Neil |date=2026-08-12 |title=Ned Lamont Wins the Democratic Primary for Connecticut Governor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/11/us/politics/connecticut-primary-governor-lamont-elliott.html |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Lamont is one of the most popular governors in the United States, with a 63% approval rating as of October 2025, according to [[Morning Consult]];<ref>{{Cite web |title=U.S. Governor Approval Rating Tracker |url=https://pro.morningconsult.com/trackers/governor-approval-ratings |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=Morning Consult Pro |language=en}}</ref> however, a [[University of New Hampshire]] poll from May 2025 found that 44% of Connecticut voters believe he should not run for a third term.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Craven |first=John |date=June 5, 2025 |title=Gov. Lamont 'seriously' considering running for a rare third term |url=https://connecticut.news12.com/gov-lamont-seriously-considering-running-for-a-rare-third-term |website=News 12 Connecticut}}</ref> [[Connecticut House of Representatives|State representative]] [[Josh Elliott (politician)|Josh Elliott]] challenged Lamont in the primary as a [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Putterman |first=Alex |title=State Rep. Josh Elliott announces campaign for governor, promising to tax CT's wealthy |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/politics/article/ct-josh-elliott-governor-lamont-primary-challenge-20768829.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260206022833/https://www.ctinsider.com/politics/article/ct-josh-elliott-governor-lamont-primary-challenge-20768829.php |archive-date=2026-02-06 |access-date=2026-02-06 |work=CT Insider |language=en}}</ref>
{{toclimit|4}}

==Democratic primary==
While incumbent [[List of governors of Connecticut|governor]] [[Ned Lamont]] initially had expressed doubts about running for a third term,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Haar |first=Dan |title=Dan Haar: Will he run? Lamont interview reveals doubts about a third term for Connecticut governor |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/politics/article/ct-gov-ned-lamont-third-term-20243961.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250701001417/https://www.ctinsider.com/politics/article/ct-gov-ned-lamont-third-term-20243961.php |archive-date=2025-07-01 |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=CT Insider |language=en}}</ref> he announced that he would run for re-election in November 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pazniokas |first=Mark |date=2025-11-14 |title=Today, the curtain goes up on Ned Lamont's bid for a third term |url=https://ctmirror.org/2025/11/14/gov-lamont-reelection-third-term-announcement/ |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=CT Mirror |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Connecticut House of Representatives|State representative]] [[Josh Elliott (politician)|Josh Elliott]] had already launched a bid to primary Lamont, believing that Connecticut needed a more [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] leader.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Craven |first=John |date=2025-07-14 |title=Democrat Josh Elliott launches bid for governor, promising big shift from Lamont |url=https://connecticut.news12.com/2025/07/14/democrat-josh-elliott-launches-bid-for-governor-promising-big-shift-from/4fXhwKnBB4lof6pdqcoKJs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518211332/https://connecticut.news12.com/2025/07/14/democrat-josh-elliott-launches-bid-for-governor-promising-big-shift-from/4fXhwKnBB4lof6pdqcoKJs |archive-date=2026-05-18 |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=News 12 Connecticut}}</ref>

At the Democratic State Convention on May 16, 2026, at [[The Bushnell Center for the Performing Arts|The Bushnell]] in [[Hartford, Connecticut|Hartford]], Lamont defeated Elliott for the [[Democratic Party of Connecticut|state party]] endorsement, 1,468 votes (74.6%) to 501 (25.4%). However, Elliott surpassed the 15% of delegates needed to get on the ballot for the primary, which took place on August 11;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Andrew |date=2026-05-16 |title=CT Dems endorse Lamont for 3rd term, but he faces primary |url=https://ctmirror.org/2026/05/16/lamont-clinches-ct-democratic-party-endorsement-but-will-face-primary/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=CT Mirror |language=en-US}}</ref> Lamont was the first incumbent governor to face a primary since [[Ella Grasso]] in [[1978 Connecticut gubernatorial election|1978]].

Lamont would go on to win the primary, and the party's endorsement.<ref name=":1" />

==Republican primary==
===Governor===
At the Republican State Convention on May 16, 2026, at Mohegan Sun in Uncasville, state Sen. [[Ryan Fazio]] (R-[[Greenwich, Connecticut|Greenwich]]) won the party's endorsement with approximately 92% of delegate votes on the first ballot. Former New York Lt. Gov. [[Betsy McCaughey]] received about 8% of the vote, falling well short of the 15% threshold needed to force an August primary, and quickly endorsed Fazio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pazniokas |first=Mark |date=2026-05-16 |title=Ryan Fazio wins the CT GOP nomination for governor |url=https://ctmirror.org/2026/05/16/ryan-fazio-wins-the-ct-gop-nomination-for-governor/ |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=CT Mirror |language=en-US}}</ref>

In the following months before the convention, [[Erin Stewart]], the former mayor of [[New Britain, Connecticut|New Britain]], was seen as the frontrunner in a tight race with Fazio. Just a day before the May 15th convention, Stewart suspended her campaign amid reports of alleged misuse of a New Britain city credit card for over $200,000 in personal expenses. Stewart subsequently endorsed Fazio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pazniokas |first=Mark |date=2026-05-16 |title=Ryan Fazio wins the CT GOP nomination for governor |url=https://ctmirror.org/2026/05/16/ryan-fazio-wins-the-ct-gop-nomination-for-governor/ |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=CT Mirror |language=en-US}}</ref>
